description:
Political Map
as the headline feature of Sector Map Layers

This is the pre-release stage intended for public testing and feedback collection.
You can try this mod early and share your experiences, so I can improve it.
Are you struggling to keep track of faction presence and growth?
Do you want to know which systems are claimed and by who before you even take the trip there?
Do you want to paint the map with your conquests?
Do you just want to see all that border gore factions in your mod list produce?
Do you want to play Bad Apple?

This mod requires LazyLib, LunaLib.
It's safe to install mid-run,
and there's a short uninstall procedure you will need to follow if you decide to keep your save after uninstalling the mod.

This mod is made compatible with Nexerelin, Fast Rendering, Random Assortment of Things.

Sector Map Layers is an overlay for the map screen (Tab, Q), the intel screen (E, 1), the minimap in the bottom right corner of the screen (replaces the vanilla radar) if you have Random Assortment of Things installed.

Examples

Map screen.

Intel screen.

Random Assortment of Things minimap.

Everything is calculated and drawn off of game data, and it gets updated as the state of the sector changes. Map layers don't alter any of the data being used to draw it, making map layers read-only by design.

Sector examples

Vanilla.

Lightly modded.

Heavily modded.

How to access map layers
KMU comes with Sector Map Layers feature turned on by default. After loading a save or starting a new game, when you open the map screen or the intel screen, you'll see a new Map layers button among map filter buttons. Clicking that button or pressing (M) enables the map layer overlay and its sidebar.

Map screen.

Intel screen.

The main control interface of map layers is the collapsible sidebar that lists all available layers and related knobs and toggles.

Available map layers
Political Map (P)
Focuses on populated colonies (markets) and their affiliation.
Only they paint the map.
Decivilised markets are treated as populated (can be disabled in settings) and aligned with Neutral faction (politically disorganised as contrasted by the Independent faction). Systems only with decivilised markets are painted in their own style (adjustable in settings).
Markets with Abandoned Station condition are treated as unpopulated and produce no map paint.
All non-market entities produce no map paint.

Examples

Unclaimed unpopulated systems are drawn very faintly just to show where systems touch.
Those outlines of unpopulated systems can be toggled on and off independently from populated systems,
which are always drawn even when there's no organised faction in the system (e.g. all colonies in a system are decivilised).
You can also adjust their visual style independently from faction and decivilised systems.

Any given system can be painted by only a single faction, so each system draws a presence ribbon hugging its border that represents each populated colony with the color of the faction holding them. Ribbons are shortened to represent solidified control when only a single faction or alliance is present in a system, while that presence is in no violation of unconditional claims.

Examples

Presence ribbons: Samarra draws one showing 3 Hegemony markets and 1 Independent market.

Expandable system tooltips provide detailed information on how each market affects the balance of power.

Examples

Tooltips list Neutral (unowned) markets.

Tooltips list markets producing no domination score.

Factions holding any population centers are listed in a sortable filter. Selecting any of them spotlights their presence across the sector. Neutral is listed there alongside organised factions, so selecting it spotlights every system holding decivilised colonies.
In domination views (Factions and Alliances) solid fill represents domination, hatched fill represents presence in a system dominated by somebody else, no fill represents claims on unpopulated systems.
On the Claims view all systems are painted with solid fill.

Examples

Faction filter, expanded to 2 columns, sorted by faction attitude toward the player.

Alliances view filtered by the Luddic Church alliance.

Factions view filtered by Pirates.

Unpopulated systems get no paint in domination views.
Tia star system is shown as Hegemony-owned because Hegemony holds an unconditional claim for it.

The Political Map comes with 3 views:
Factions - paints faction territory based on a custom domination algorithm (highly customisable in settings) that weighs markets sizes, stability, whether a market is hidden, presence of an orbital station (or if a station is militarised), and the number of patrol fleets generated (by their sizes).

Examples

Luddic Church unconditionally claims Penelope's Star but isn't present there,
and per domination rules actually present faction (Independent) reads as the holder.
The claim is still listed in the tooltip.

Alliances (only visible with Nexerelin installed) - same as Factions but allied factions stand as a single political entity with their holdings combined.

Examples

Tooltips in the Alliances view combine domination score of present alliance members.

Claims - paints faction territory based on the vanilla system claim mechanic - dynamic or unconditional. Unconditional claims are set via sector memory and are the highest authority. Unless a claim is unconditional, system claim is resolved dynamically - the single biggest market (that participates in the economy) wins, boosted by the presence of same-faction markets (of any kind) and any military industry constructed. The player faction and non-territorial factions cannot lay claims dynamically. If you filter by a non-territorial faction, unclaimed systems with their presence will be spotlit.

Examples

Luddic Church isn't present in Penelope's Star system, holds an unconditional claim on it,
and there's a non-territorial faction (Independent) present.

Spoiler protection
To avoid spoilers, map layers operate on a vanilla-derived visibility system (each component is available in settings):
Hidden systems (with no hyperspace anchor generated off of a star, nebula, or a black hole) are not revealed unless there's a visible population center present or it holds an active gate.
Entities marked as discoverable (hidden on the system map until in range of player fleet sensors) are not revealed. They are also listed on Claims tooltips because vanilla uses them in claim calculations, but are redacted.
Markets marked as hidden are not revealed if there are no visible colonies held by other non-allied factions, or until the player visits their system. They are also listed on Claims tooltips because vanilla uses them in claim calculations, but are redacted.
Decivilised markets are not revealed unless they start so, or until the player performs a full survey on them (adjustable in settings). These markets are also revealed if there are visible colonies held by other non-allied factions.
Unowned markets with the Abandoned Station condition follow visibility rules of hidden markets.

This mod comes with a suite of LunaLib settings that allow you to tweak, visuals, sound volume, keybinds, underlying mechanics.

Console commands
If you've got Console Commands installed you can make use of the following commands.

Provided by KMU:
kmu_profiling [tree|flat|walks] [namespace=<prefix>] [top=<count>] [perframe] [reset] - Writes full or scoped performance measurements to game logs on demand. Calls exceeding the budget are logged automatically without this command. Requires profiling to be enabled in settings.

Provided by KMLib:
kmlib_activate_gate <id> - Activates the gate with that id in the current system.
kmlib_colonise [entity-id] [faction-id] - Founds a colony. [entity-id] defaults to the nearest colonisable market. [faction-id] defaults to the player faction.
kmlib_list_factions [markets|hidden|discoverable|no_markets] [no_holdings] [no_attitude] [to_log] - Lists every faction with what it holds - how many places, how many hidden, how many discoverable, and the systems they sit in. By default no filter is applied.
kmlib_list_map_spoilers - Lists faction-owned systems as a tree of system, entities and factions, flagging cut-off systems and undiscovered markets.
kmlib_list_system_entities [gates] - Lists the current system's entities as an orbit tree, then the unorbited ones and fleets with coordinates. By default the [gates] filter is not applied.
kmlib_spawn <gate|jump_point> [orbit_focus_id] [speed] [jitter=<frac>] - Spawns a gate or a jump point at the fleet position. [orbit_focus_id] defaults to system center. [speed] is derived from radius by default. [jitter] defaults to 0.25.
kmlib_transfer_market [entity-id] [faction-id] - Hands an existing colony to another owner. [entity-id] defaults to the nearest colonisable market. [faction-id] defaults to the player faction.

Compatibility
KMU injects map layers into the map widget as map-only terrain. And to be visible in the Starscape mode, the starscape terrain variant is tagged as a slipstream. Custom terrain is the only thing that has to be serialised into saves as Java class references, and that's why a clean uninstall is required for disabling the mod.

The game reuses the map widget, and so do many mods. Those custom placements of the widget get map layers for free, but they should come with no mouseover detection and no controls (borrowing selections from the map screen as the main instance) without a compatibility patch.

Additionally, the mod has been made specifically compatible with:
Fast Rendering from v0.9.1rc1 on, which answers the map's cursor read itself. On an older release the map stops following the cursor, and a notice names the release to update to.
Nexerelin to support its alliance mechanics.
Random Assortment of Things and its minimap replacement. The minimap draws the map widget via a tooltip in the corner of the screen. This mod comes with a RAT compatibility mode enabled by default that scopes mouse detection to the widget. Layer selection is inherited from the map screen. As a bonus, the map widget is made invisible when it's docked off-screen (docking is RAT's way of hiding the map widget when the player docks at markets or opens any UI screens) - that disables any related rendering and should provide a marginal performance improvement (more so when in hyperspace) in the menus that don't show the sector map.

While playing with this pre-release, please report if you think it relates to this mod:

what kind of visual or technical issues you've got,
how's your performance,
how's your user experience,
if you see mod incompatibilities or if the map ignores any modded content,
if the map spoils anything you think it's not supposed to.

Diagnostics options:

The DEBUG logging level in both KMLib and KMU dev settings. To write all internal mod logs.
A reflection logs toggle in KMU dev settings. To trace issues interacting with vanilla UI.
Profiling toggle and level in KMU map dev settings combined with usage of kmu_profiling console command. To trace where performance drops occur.

You can try breaking the mod or just play as you normally would.

And feel free to share suggestions, ideas, requests - those will affect this mod's direction and priorities. While I have ideated and planned out some info-layers I want to implement next, and some of their conception - that covers my own vision, and I'd like to hear what's yours.

Post-release roadmap
Vanilla intel integration into the visibility system.
Map layer help tooltips.
Faction and alliance tooltips off of the sortable filter list.
Filling in wedges and gaps between system cells.
Processing non-market entities and showing what's visible on system tooltips.
Incorporating some modded entities into the domination algorithm, like watchtowers and artillery implemented in Industrial Evolution.
A diplomatic map derived from the political map but focused on relations.
An Enemies view that paints the map by the lowest relations in a system, and a Friends view that paints only systems with factions above a chosen threshold.
Targets player faction relations by default, and applying the faction filter applies the focus to a specific faction.
Presence ribbons are painted with relation colors instead of faction colors.
The political map is extended with Friends and Enemies filter recede modes - when a faction filter is applied, the rest of the sector paints relations instead of being muted or desaturated.

An infrastructure map focused on non-market entities. For example a comm relay network view that shows detected network coverage.
An economy map focused on markets, industries, and commodities.
A faction management layer focused on player faction markets and fleets.
A framework for modders defining and supplying their own custom layers based on existing ones or brand new.

AI usage disclaimer
this mod has been made with usage of LLMs - for research, brainstorming, code generation, code review, code refactoring, translation. Each step was performed with human oversight and playtesting, with as much human code review as can be reasonably performed for a mod project.

The Simplified Chinese translation has been done using the following technique. Vanilla vocabulary was matched to the Chinese core localisation, and other mods' vocabulary to their own Chinese versions. Forum vocabulary was collected as well, and all of it was gathered into a translation reference that records the rationale for each term. KMLib's and KMU's own vocabulary was translated by the intent behind each term. The mod author reviewed all the collected vocabulary against those rationales, and the translations were applied in several passes for consistency.

Thanks:
To the Fractal Softworks team for bringing us Starsector and continuously improving it.
To the modding community for producing awesome and inspiring mods that bring me back to Starsector every time.
To developers and maintainers of LazyLib, LunaLib, Console Commands for providing features this mod relies on.
To developers and maintainers of Nexerelin for bringing the politics of the sector to life.
To Genir for implementing a more stable compatibility solution in Fast Rendering.
To awesome folks over at Fractal Softworks forums, at r/Starsector, and in Discord communities for feedback and support.

discordPostHtml:
Currently in pre-release. Requires LazyLib and LunaLib. Safe to enable mid-save, uninstalled via settings.

Install it via TriOS or by downloading KMLib (its dependency) and KMU (the mod itself).

The Political Map is the first among Sector Map Layers and focuses on populated colonies and their allegiances, with Faction, Alliance, and Claim views. It shows up primarily on the map screen and the intel screen, with a collapsible sidebar as its control interface.

Made compatible with Fast Rendering, Nexerelin (alliances), Random Assortment of Things (minimap replacement). Can play Bad Apple.

Bishop1664 made a short video showcase.

Discuss in https://discord.com/channels/187635036525166592/1549091275167240272
Forum thread: https://fractalsoftworks.com/forum/index.php?topic=36029.0
aiDescription: Adds an overlay to the map and intel screens that visualizes faction presence, claims, and domination across the sector. It includes a Political Map layer with views for Factions, Alliances, and Claims, using a custom domination algorithm or vanilla claim mechanics. The overlay features presence ribbons, expandable tooltips, and spoiler protection based on vanilla visibility rules.
